name: Mombasa port strike — Pune to Nairobi vaccine lane
description: A 240,000-dose vaccine container is on the water when Mombasa goes on strike. The schedule clock and the stability clock diverge, which is what makes the answer interesting. A second shipment suffers a sustained freeze so there is a Critical disposition for a human to sign - and for Bob to be refused on.

events.text: Calm. Everything in range, clocks green.
Doors open at the Jebel Ali transhipment. Planned handling - a short blip the sanity rules absorb, so the later alarm is believed.

events.headline: Mombasa port workers begin indefinite strike; berthing suspended
events.text: The disruption Bob raises from a pasted headline.
Reefer compressor fails while the vessel waits offshore. The cargo starts warming toward ambient - this is what the breach predictor catches before 8 C is crossed.

Unrelated unit overcools a thawed mRNA consignment and holds it below -0.5 C for over an hour. Freeze on a freeze-sensitive product is irreversible: Critical, quarantine, QA/RP signature required. This is the case Bob tries to sign and is refused.
Rescue reefer plugged in after dispatch - the stability clock stops draining.

notes: Timings are in simulated minutes from the start of the run. At 60x, minute 72 is 72 minutes of shipment time, about 1.2 hours.

Nothing here sets a severity, a clock value or a disposition. Those are computed by the engines from the readings this scenario produces - which is why npm run record and npm run demo show the same numbers.
